Wi-Fi coverage in real workspaces

Indoor beacon measurements across 32 locations produced a path-loss model capturing distance and wall attenuation with R² = 0.93.

At a glance

Measure how a real building reshapes wireless coverage.

Wi-FiWiresharkRegressionPath loss
Experiment

A monitor-mode WLAN card captured roughly 300 beacon frames at each of 32 locations inside an IIT Madras workspace. Distance from the access point, intervening walls, and RSSI were recorded across workspaces and floors.

Model & evidence

The fitted log-distance model used a reference RSSI of −31.3 dBm, a path-loss exponent of 2.81, and wall attenuation near −3.03 dB per wall.

Result

The fit reached R² = 0.93. Signal strength followed expected logarithmic distance decay, while obstacles materially shifted readings. In this environment, staying within roughly ten metres helped maintain stronger-than −65 dBm coverage; elevated placement and line of sight were beneficial.
